Twelve persons sit in two parallel rows of six persons each, one row behind the other. All of them face north and Row 1 is in front of Row 2, so each person in Row 2 sits directly behind a person in Row 1. The persons are A, B, C, D, E, F, P, Q, R, S, T and U, not necessarily in the same order.

4. C sits directly behind R.
5. B sits second to the right of the one who sits second to the right of Q.
6. R is an immediate neighbour of P.
7. B sits third to the right of T.
8. U sits to the immediate left of S.
9. D does not sit at any of the extreme ends of the row.

Clue 8 cannot be met in Case 1, Case 2, Case 3 and Case 4, so they are rejected.
Clues 8, 4 and 3 then place Eshwar, Suresh, Imran and Pranav.
Clue 9 cannot be met in Case 6, so it is rejected.
Clues 9 and 10 then place Kabir and Geeta.

solution.shortcut: Count the seats strictly between the two persons — not the persons themselves.
solution.trap: Two comes from counting one of the two named persons.
